title: Person::clients counts a client once per shared room
description:
Found by the review of branch irc-verbs, not by the bead that added the
field (mimid-1wgh.140.5).

sync::refresh_clients (crates/mimid-agent-store/src/sync.rs) walks every
room and every client in it, incrementing per (room, client):

  for room in agent.rooms() { for client in agent.clients(&room.uri) {
      *counted.entry(user).or_default() += 1 } }

There is no per-user deduplication of clients across rooms, so one
device in five shared rooms is stored as clients: Some(5), and two
devices in three rooms as Some(6).

Person::clients (crates/mimid-agent-store/src/record.rs) says "How many
of this user's clients are leaves of the MLS group of a room this user
shares with them". That is a public, serialized record field any front
end may read, so the contract is wrong, not just a helper.

No reply is wrong today: monitor::Session::verdict only tests count > 0,
and MONITOR is the only reader. That is why this is P3 and not P2 -- but
the next reader of the field inherits a number that means nothing.

Two ways out, and the choice is the point of the bead:
- Count each client once: collect per-room client URIs into a
  BTreeMap<String, BTreeSet<String>> of user to client id and store the
  set's length. Then the field means what it says.
- Or redefine it as leaves across shared groups, counting a client once
  per shared room, and say so at the field, in the crate docs and in
  agent-frontends.md §7.39.

Either way the test belongs with it: a contact sharing two rooms with
one device, asserting the number the chosen reading gives. The existing
test (mimid-agent-store tests/groundwork.rs
a_person_record_counts_the_clients_in_a_shared_group) uses one room, so
it cannot tell the two readings apart.
